title: Open problem: Zero-one law for directional transience in dimensions d >= 3
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For a RWRE satisfying (E) and (IID) and any direction l, is P_0[A_l] in {0,1}, where A_l is the event of transience in direction l? Known for d = 1 and d = 2 (Zerner-Merkl). Source: Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment, Open question 3.2, p. 42.
Posed in Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

title: Attempt on Zero-one law for directional transience in dimensions d >= 3
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Analyse where the Zerner-Merkl planar argument uses d = 2. Result: Zerner-Merkl show P_0[A_l intersection A_{-l}] = 0 using that in d = 2 two independent walks in the same environment started at distant points on a line perpendicular to l must, with positive probability, have paths that intersect (planarity), which lets one derive a contradiction from the walk going to +infinity and -infinity in direction l with positive probability each. In d >= 3 paths of two walks need not intersect, and the known partial result (Kalikow's 0-1 law: P_0[A_l union A_{-l}] in {0,1}) does not exclude the mixed event. A candidate counterexample structure in d >= 3 would be an i.i.d. environment where the walk is guided to +l or -l depending on a local feature it meets first; the i.i.d. assumption and the fact that the walk visits infinitely many independent regions make such a persistent memory implausible but not provably impossible: the walk in direction +l sees fresh environment forever, and the event that it turns around is a tail event of the walk but not of the environment. I checked that the natural martingale argument (P_omega(A_l) as a function of the environment at the current position) fails because P_omega(A_l) is not measurable with respect to a finite region. No result. Obstruction: Planarity is essential to the d = 2 proof; no substitute in d >= 3.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0044-zero-one-law-for-directional-transience-in-dimensions-d-3
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

title: Technique: Kalikow's Zero-One Law
body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Kalikow's zero-one law (1981; Zerner-Merkl 2001 for the sharp form): for random walk in an i.i.d. elliptic random environment on Z^d and a direction l, let A_l = {X_n . l -> +infinity}. Then P_0(A_l union A_{-l}) is 0 or 1. It does NOT say that P_0(A_l) itself is 0 or 1: the directional zero-one law P_0(A_l) in {0,1} is a theorem in d = 1 (Solomon) and d = 2 (Zerner-Merkl, using planarity: two walks in the same environment must intersect), and is an OPEN PROBLEM for d >= 3 (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 3.2; Kalikow's law is often misquoted as the directional one). Kalikow's proof: the event A_l union A_{-l} is invariant under a coupling of walks started at different points that follow the same environment after they meet in a slab, and its probability is a function of the environment's tail sigma-field, hence 0 or 1 by Kolmogorov. Consequences: under transience in some direction the regeneration structure of Sznitman-Zerner applies to the union event; Zerner's law of large numbers then gives X_n/n -> v or -c v. Typical failure: Treating Kalikow's zero-one law as if it determines transience, mistaking the statement that the probability is 0 or 1 for a claim that it equals 1; the theorem only rules out intermediate probabilities and leaves open, often genuinely unresolved, which side of the dichotomy holds for a specific environment law, which is precisely the content of the still largely open general ballisticity conjecture for random walk in random environment in dimension d>=2. Canonical reference: Kalikow, 1981, Annals of Probability; Zeitouni, 2004, Ecole d'Ete de Probabilites de Saint-Flour, Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics.
i.i.d. (or stationary ergodic with care) elliptic environment on Z^d
The statement concerns the UNION of the two directional events
Directional 0-1 law is open for d >= 3

title: Attempt on Uniqueness of planar directional geodesics in every fixed direction
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Uniqueness of planar directional geodesics in every fixed direction structural argument Result: A full-measure deterministic set may omit the axis, for example[0,2pi) without0. Also, a random exceptional set can be nonempty almost surely while excluding each fixed angle almost surely: a singleton containing an independent uniform angle has this property. Check: The first example checks the deterministic exceptional-set issue. In the second, P(U=theta)=0 for every fixed theta but the singleton is never empty. Obstruction: Fubini-based almost-every-direction arguments do not settle even a prescribed exceptional angle. A geometric argument sensitive to that direction is needed.

title: Attempt on Coalescence of directional FPP rays in higher dimensions
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Coalescence of directional FPP rays in higher dimensions structural argument Result: Translation invariance and one outgoing edge at every vertex do not force coalescence. Orient every edge line in the positive e1 direction in Z^d. There is exactly one forward ray from each vertex, but rays on different parallel lines never meet. Check: The construction is deterministic and translation invariant. All rays have the same asymptotic direction, so directional agreement alone adds no coalescence. Obstruction: This is a forest counterexample to a proof strategy, not the iid FPP model. Planar shielding and ordering used in the source proof do not extend automatically.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0115-coalescence-of-directional-fpp-rays-in-higher-dimensions

title: Attempt on Zero-one law for directional transience in dimensions d >= 3 (corrected)
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD (SUPERSEDING REVISION 2026-09-07 12:4x after the Codex holder's review), author-checked only. CORRECTION of C0044-A001's first sentence. The events {X_n . l -> +infinity} and {X_n . l -> -infinity} are disjoint by definition, so 'Zerner-Merkl show P(A_l intersect A_{-l}) = 0' is empty; what Zerner-Merkl prove in d = 2 is P_0(A_l) in {0,1}, using planarity to show two walks in the same environment intersect, which is what A001 then describes. The reduction (planarity essential; no d >= 3 substitute; no finite-region measurability for the natural martingale) stands. Key identity: Zerner-Merkl (d=2): P_0(A_l) in {0,1}; Kalikow (all d): P_0(A_l union A_{-l}) in {0,1}; d >= 3 directional law open. Standing obstruction: see the earlier attempt; the correction above replaces the flawed step only.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0044-zero-one-law-for-directional-transience-in-dimensions-d-3

title: Directional Malliavin Derivatives on Wiener-Poisson Space
body:
The Malliavin derivative on the Wiener-Poisson space is defined as the closed unbounded operator D = (D^{(1)}, D^{(2)}): D^{1, 2} subset L^2(Omega) -> L^2([0, T] x Omega) x L^2([0, T] x R_0 x Omega). For F in D^{(1)}, D_t^{(1)} F represents the stochastic gradient in the Brownian direction defined via directional perturbations along Cameron-Martin paths. For F in D^{(2)} with chaotic expansion F = sum_{n=0}^infinity I_n(h_n) with respect to Poisson integrals, D_{t, z}^{(2)} F = sum_{n=1}^infinity n * I_{n-1}(h_n(t, ., z)) denotes the difference operator F(omega + delta_{(t, z)}) - F(omega). The Hilbert space domain D^{1, 2} is equipped with the graph norm ||F||_{D^{1, 2}}^2 = ||F||_{L^2}^2 + ||D^{(1)} F||_{L^2([0, T] x Omega)}^2 + ||D^{(2)} F||_{L^2([0, T] x R_0 x Omega)}^2.
F in D^{1, 2} = D^{(1)} cap D^{(2)}
